content: Ribavirin, marketed under the brand name REBETOL, is a synthetic nucleoside analogue, specifically a purine analogue. Its chemical name is 1-β-D-ribofuranosyl-1H-1,2,4-triazole-3-carboxamide. Ribavirin appears as a white, crystalline powder that is freely soluble in water and slightly soluble in anhydrous alcohol. REBETOL capsules contain 200 mg of ribavirin as the active ingredient. The capsules are composed of a white powder enclosed in a white, opaque, gelatin capsule. The inactive ingredients in the capsule include microcrystalline cellulose, lactose monohydrate, croscarmellose sodium, and magnesium stearate. The capsule shell is made of gelatin, sodium lauryl sulfate, silicon dioxide, and titanium dioxide. The capsule is printed with edible blue pharmaceutical ink, which is composed of shellac, anhydrous ethyl alcohol, isopropyl alcohol, n-butyl alcohol, propylene glycol, ammonium hydroxide, and FD&C Blue 2 aluminum lake. REBETOL is also available as an oral solution, which is a clear, colorless to pale or light yellow liquid with a bubble gum flavor. Each milliliter of the solution contains 40 mg of ribavirin. The inactive ingredients in the oral solution include sucrose, glycerin, sorbitol, propylene glycol, sodium citrate, citric acid, sodium benzoate, natural and artificial bubble gum flavoring (identified as 15864), and water.
